clue.text: Key a retired factory worker has left for safe-keeping

indicators.note: something held for safe-keeping is kept inside, so the outer pieces hold the others

parts.note: the ant is the classic worker insect

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the word for the factory is read backwards

parts.note: a mill is a factory
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A pensioned-off factory hand has deposited something for safe-keeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' reverses the factory word, and 'has ... for safe-keeping' makes A + the worker hold the rest. 'Key' is an adjective here, not something for a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: Key in the adjectival sense means crucial or of the utmost significance.

clue.text: Structure made with expert technique

parts.note: arch as an adjective means cunning or expert, as in an arch manipulator
a way of doing something is a technique or method

explanation.surface: A building put up by someone with real skill and method.
explanation.definitionFit: An arched passage or entrance is a kind of built structure.

clue.text: Council's Good Pub Guide?

definitions.meaning: a council, with the 's read as 'is', is a body governing a town or district
read cryptically, an expert on locals, i.e. neighbourhood pubs, which in Britain are called 'locals'

explanation.surface: A town council publishes a guide to the best pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A district council is the body governing a local area; the cryptic reading is an expert on local pubs.

clue.text: With this I can spot rubbish!

definitions.meaning: the organ a speaker uses to see things
an exclamation of disbelief, meaning nonsense

explanation.surface: A boast about having a sharp eye for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: 'My eye!' is an old exclamation of scorn meaning nonsense, and an eye is what one sees with.

clue.text: Enrolled for series of lectures, making progress as expected

definitions.meaning: signed up to a programme of study, literally on a course
proceeding according to plan, on track

explanation.surface: A student signs up for a lecture series and is doing as well as hoped.
explanation.definitionFit: Being signed up for a programme of study and being on track for a goal share the same phrase.

clue.text: Report cut in incidental expenses

indicators.note: the answer is a piece cut out of the words that follow, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: An account of spending trimmed back within petty-cash costs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale is a story or account, as a report of events is.

clue.text: Worker keeps right on supporting miners' leader

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports another sits beneath it in the grid

parts.note: the NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers in Britain

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the worker's word wraps the next pieces

parts.note: the bee is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A loyal employee carries on backing the head of the miners' union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miners' leader' looks like one phrase, but miners' gives NUM and 'leader' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The number one in an organisation is its chief or leader.

clue.text: Here you can get gallon, if it isn't going bust

indicators.note: going bust suggests breaking up, so these letters fall apart and are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A petrol station that will sell you a gallon unless it goes out of business.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of GALLON IF IT ISN'T are rearranged; the whole clue also describes the place, where you buy fuel by the gallon.
explanation.definitionFit: A filling station is a petrol station, the place where you can get fuel.

clue.text: Mean crime by character that's unknown

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick or swindle, a crime
y is one of the letters used for an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A nasty offence committed by a mysterious figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy means mean in the sense of tight-fisted and ungenerous.

clue.text: The age of the bike?

definitions.meaning: a ... can be a long era or age

explanation.surface: A question about when bicycles first came along.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle is both a long period of time and a bicycle.

clue.text: Contributor to newspaper, totally lacking in energy, composed one Times clue

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the remaining letters are rearranged
energy is E, and totally lacking means every such letter is taken out

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer, completely drained, has written a single clue for The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'totally lacking in energy' removes all three Es from ONE TIMES CLUE, leaving ONTIMSCLU; 'composed' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A columnist writes a regular column, so is a contributor to a newspaper.

clue.text: Breaking law, gets taken before the beak and imprisoned

indicators.note: breaking suggests smashing, so the letters of law are rearranged

parts.note: led means taken or guided along, as a prisoner is
to be up before the beak is to appear in court; beak is British slang for a magistrate

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker is hauled in front of a magistrate and locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' rearranges the letters of the clue word. BEAK is British slang for a magistrate, so being 'up before the beak' means appearing in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Walled up means shut in behind walls, enclosed and confined like a prisoner.

clue.text: According to reports, Garden City is favourably situated

indicators.note: reports are what is heard, so the place name is said aloud

parts.note: Welwyn Garden City is a planned town in Hertfordshire, England

explanation.surface: A planned English town is said to be in a good location.
explanation.walkthrough: WELWYN Garden City is a planned town north of London; spoken, Welwyn sounds like the phrase meaning well placed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be well in is to be in a favourable position, especially with someone influential.

clue.text: Delinquent guys, note, can be most immature

indicators.note: delinquent means misbehaving, so the letters of guys and note are rearranged

explanation.surface: Juvenile offenders are often the least grown-up.
explanation.definitionFit: The youngest are the least mature, superlative for superlative.

clue.text: Insular character working in a garden

indicators.note: working suggests being worked over and changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An islander busy tending a garden plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A Grenadian comes from the Caribbean island of Grenada, so is an island person, an insular character.

clue.text: Fellow's aim to visit northern city endlessly put back

indicators.note: put back means returned the other way, so the whole assembly is read backwards
visiting means going inside, so one piece sits within the other
endlessly means with its final letter cut off

parts.note: York is a city in the north of England
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A man plans to go to a northern city but keeps postponing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims the city, 'to visit' puts the aim inside it, giving YENDOR, and 'put back' reads that backwards. 'Fellow's' is the definition with 's as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodney is a man's name, so stands for a fellow; the 's is read as 'is'.

clue.text: Food makes sailor complain

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
to beef is slang for to grumble or complain

explanation.surface: Grub that gets a seaman grumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt beef is beef cured in brine, a traditional food, not least at sea.

clue.text: Bank employee hasn't entered shillings in notebook

indicators.note: here the letter for shillings has not gone in, so it is left out of the bank worker

parts.note: a cashier works at a bank counter
s is the abbreviation for shillings in old British money

explanation.surface: A bank clerk has failed to write the shillings into a ledger.
explanation.walkthrough: S for shilling comes from pre-decimal British currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A cahier is a notebook or exercise book, from French.

clue.text: Game for starters served in dish

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Game for starters served in dish (3,3)': CUTIE (dish) takes a P, but no clue word supplies it; the clue looks cut short in OCR and no source gives the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Game for starters served in dish

clue.text: Behaved amorously, being cuddled by knave, perhaps

indicators.note: being cuddled means held in the arms, so this piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the knave or jack is an example of a playing card
esse is Latin for being, existence

explanation.surface: Someone got romantic while held in the arms of a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knave, perhaps' looks like a rogue, but is a playing card. ESSE, Latin for 'to be', is a common crossword word for being.
explanation.definitionFit: To caress is to stroke tenderly, so caressed means behaved amorously.

clue.text: One's taking tablets as told after onset of debilitating illness

indicators.note: after puts the onset letter first, ahead of the pieces the clue gives earlier
onset is the start, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: one's read as I's, that is one is, giving IS

indicators.note: told means spoken, so the letters for tablets are pronounced

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so tablets are Es

explanation.surface: Someone on medication as prescribed after the first signs of a weakening disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as told' says ES, ecstasy tablets, aloud as EASE. 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease is an illness or disorder of the body.

clue.text: Where some youths might loiter like hoodies

parts.note: teenagers often hang about in a park
as means like, in the manner of

explanation.surface: Hooded teenagers lurking about in their usual haunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkas are hooded jackets, so hoodies in the sense of hooded tops.

clue.text: Having only one pound, stop going to bars in English city

indicators.note: having only one means one of the two matching letters is removed

parts.note: to stall is to stop or come to a halt
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from libra
bans are prohibitions, things that bar

explanation.surface: Short of money, someone gives up the pub crawl in an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having only one pound' drops one L from STALL; ST ALBANS is a cathedral city in Hertfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: St Albans is a cathedral city in Hertfordshire, England.

clue.text: Told one to quit the bar

indicators.note: told means said out loud, so the word for someone leaving is pronounced

parts.note: a leaver is someone who quits or departs

explanation.surface: Someone was ordered out of the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but the definition is a rigid bar used for prising.
explanation.definitionFit: A lever is a rigid bar pivoted to move a load.

clue.text: Writer succeeded with a succinct version of "The King and I"

parts.note: s is the standard abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

parts.words: succinct version of "The King and I"
parts.note: the title shortened to its key letters, K for king and I

explanation.surface: An author made it big with a cut-down production of a famous musical.
explanation.walkthrough: K is the chess abbreviation for king.
explanation.definitionFit: Saki was the pen name of H. H. Munro, the British short-story writer.

clue.text: Complex in California, dull on the outside

indicators.note: the word for dull sits on the outside, wrapping the state's abbreviation

parts.note: trite means dull and hackneyed
CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A building complex in California, drab from the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' looks like a noun, a group of buildings, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Intricate means complex, with many interconnected parts.

clue.text: Here you are putting fuel into vehicle mostly

indicators.note: into means the fuel goes inside the shortened vehicle
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: A garage attendant says 'there you go' while filling up most of the van.
explanation.definitionFit: Voila, from French, is said when presenting something, like 'here you are'.

clue.text: Lack of interest in a point at issue

parts.note: a difference is a disagreement, a point in dispute

explanation.surface: Not caring about a matter under debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Indifference is a lack of interest or concern.
